summary: In calendar 2025 Millrose took the share of its invested capital outside the Lennar Master Program Agreement from zero at the Feb 2025 spin to about 28% ($2.37B of $8.47B) by year end, funding $2.6B under Other Agreements against a target raised three times ($1.0B, $1.5B, $2.2B). The price gap is the headline: Lennar paid a weighted-average 8.5% all year while Other Agreements earned 11.7%, 11.4%, 11.3% and 11.0% at successive quarter ends, so the premium over Lennar narrowed from about 320 bps to about 250 bps as volume scaled; Millrose says only that newer counterparties generally pay more than Lennar, and Lennar holds a most-favoured-rate right on future assets. The Other Agreements bucket is less third-party than it looks: it includes Lennar Related Ventures and about $330M of 12% development loans, and truly independent counterparties produced only $69.4M (12%) of 2025 option fees. Only two non-Lennar builders are named in the 2025 filings, New Home Co (Landsea, $494.5M for 4,186 homesites with a deposit of about 5.4%) and Taylor Morrison's Yardly build-to-rent program via Kennedy Lewis; the other counterparties (12 in total at Sep 30, 15 at Dec 31 with 9 in the top 25) are not named. Structurally, 96% of the investment balance sits in cross-termination pools, non-Lennar deals run shorter (2.0 years remaining life vs 3.3 for Lennar), and 2026 growth (up to $2B net new) is capped by a 33% debt-to-capital ceiling and a promise not to issue equity below book.

facts.fact: Cross-termination pooling: at 2025-12-31, 96% of Millrose's portfolio investment balance was in pooling arrangements. If a counterparty lets its option lapse on one pooled property it forfeits the option deposits for the whole pool and Millrose may terminate the options on the other pooled properties and sell them free of the option. Pools are built to mix geographies, communities and product types.
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 Business

facts.fact: At 2025-06-30 all Lennar assets were pooled and 55 communities outside the Lennar Master Program Agreement were pooled for cross-termination, per the Q2 deck's pooling slide (the Q1 deck had said no third-party assets were pooled).

facts.fact: Under the Lennar Master Program Agreement, Lennar's payment obligations are capped at $50M per pool for spin-off assets and $25M per pool for other admitted properties (the 10-K does not spell out which payments the cap covers). A Lennar party can cure a default by electing a bulk purchase of the affected property, which cancels cross-termination rights already exercised.
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 Business

facts.fact: Option deposits are non-refundable, fully earned at signing, set as a percentage of the land purchase price in each agreement, and credited against the takedown price; the percentage is not disclosed for Lennar or anyone else. Takedown price is land acquisition cost plus the pre-agreed development budget funded by Millrose; the builder bears overruns above the agreed maximum and must finish land development even if it walks.
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 Business

facts.fact: Lennar pause rights: the Master Option Agreement allows pause periods of up to six months each (two periods per the risk factors) in a significant market decline or public-health emergency, during which takedown deadlines are extended and Lennar's monthly option payment can drop to 50% of the applicable rate. The 10-K also lists a Lennar right to designate a pause period.
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 Business

facts.fact: Investment guidelines in the management agreement: no more than 40% of the real estate portfolio's value in one state; limited discretionary entitlement risk; a construction agreement with cost-overrun guarantees and an option agreement with a defined takedown schedule at closing; single-family detached or attached product only; an environmental assessment no older than 180 days. No single-counterparty or single-metro limit is stated.
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 Business

facts.fact: Lennar's continuing rights: a 'Capital Priority Right' reserving part of Millrose's available capital for future Lennar-designated acquisitions and development (amount not stated), approval over any financing that would take debt-to-equity above 1:1, and a consent right over mixing Lennar-related assets into a shared collateral pool. Millrose's own leverage ceiling is 33% debt-to-capitalization.
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 Business

facts.fact: Accounting and credit: option contracts are treated as sales-type leases under ASC 842 because exercise is considered reasonably certain; option fee income is recognized on an effective-yield basis. Millrose reported no delinquencies, defaults or option terminations in 2025 and judged credit loss on the option assets immaterial; the only allowance is $1.0M on development loans.
